system_description.narrative_title: Tech decoupling and resource contest in the US–China rivalry
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an accelerating strategic decoupling between China and Western technology ecosystems driven by export controls, investment blocks, and reciprocal Chinese restrictions. Governments are using export rules, deal approvals and legal tools while firms reroute supply chains, pile up semiconductors, and seek alternative mineral sources — producing market volatility and geopolitical spillovers. China responds by expanding control over critical minerals and selectively blocking foreign deals, while Western firms and lawmakers tighten access to AI, chips and robotics. The result is an open, multi-directional system of flows (products, capital, data, talent) being reconfigured by policy levers and corporate responses.
system_description.scope: State policies and export controls (US, China, allied states); multinational firms in semiconductors, AI, robotics and mining (e.g., Nvidia, SK Hynix, SoftBank, Solvay, Samsung); global supply chains for chips, data-centre hardware and critical minerals; financial markets and investor sentiment; regulatory and legal actions affecting cross‑border deals and technology flows.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic order driven by US–China strategic rivalry and technological dominance competition
adjacent_subsystems: Global capital markets and investor risk/flows
Critical minerals and global mining geopolitics
East and Southeast Asian regional security and diplomacy
International tech governance and export-control regimes (AI, chips, dual-use)

variables.name: Export control tightness
variables.description: The degree of restrictiveness and scope of rules limiting the outbound transfer of technologies and dual‑use goods.

variables.name: FDI screening intensity
variables.description: The strictness and frequency of scrutiny applied to incoming foreign direct investment and cross‑border corporate deals in strategic sectors.

variables.name: Cross‑border trade flow
variables.description: The volume and rate of transnational shipments of components, finished tech products and intermediate goods across borders.

variables.name: Cross‑border capital flow
variables.description: The rate and volume of financial flows used for investment, mergers, acquisitions and capital allocation across jurisdictions in tech sectors.

variables.name: Data flow restrictions
variables.description: The extent to which legal, technical or policy measures limit cross‑border transfers and processing of data.

variables.name: Supply chain concentration
variables.description: The degree to which production stages, suppliers or materials for key technologies are concentrated in a narrow set of locations or actors.

variables.name: Semiconductor production capacity
variables.description: The total fabrication and packaging throughput available globally for advanced and legacy semiconductor nodes.

variables.name: Chip inventory levels
variables.description: The aggregate stockpiles of semiconductor inventory held by manufacturers, distributors and end users.

variables.name: Critical mineral share
variables.description: The proportion of global production or reserves of strategically important minerals controlled by a limited set of producers or regions.

variables.name: Resource nationalism
variables.description: The propensity of jurisdictions to assert ownership, restrict export or prioritize domestic allocation of natural resources and processing capacity.

variables.name: Firm restructuring rate
variables.description: The speed and frequency at which firms reorganize supply chains, relocate production or change sourcing and partnership arrangements.

variables.name: Deal‑blocking activity
variables.description: The occurrence and intensity of administrative or legal interventions that delay, condition or prevent cross‑border transactions in technology sectors.

variables.name: Investor volatility
variables.description: The variability of investor behaviour and financial market responses to news, policy changes and risk perceptions in technology markets.

variables.name: Technology transfer risk
variables.description: The perceived and actual probability that knowledge, intellectual property or sensitive capabilities will be transferred beyond intended controls.

variables.name: Talent mobility flow
variables.description: The rate and direction of movement of skilled researchers, engineers and technical personnel across borders and between organizations.

variables.name: Geopolitical tension
variables.description: The overall intensity of strategic rivalry and political friction that shapes policy choices and cross‑border interactions in the technological domain.

catalysts.title: Congressional hearing for Nvidia CEO
catalysts.description: U.S. lawmakers have summoned Jensen Huang to brief Congress on Chinese spying concerns; a hearing is likely imminent and could shape policy and enforcement.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US lawmakers summon Jensen Huang over Chinese spying concerns' — likely congressional scrutiny driving tighter controls and market reaction.

catalysts.title: China withholds approvals for Nvidia chip imports
catalysts.description: Beijing's delays/withholds of import approvals for Nvidia chips are ongoing, creating inventory pile-ups and trade disruptions between China and global suppliers.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia chips pile up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval' and 'Nvidia orders data centre clients to reduce China exposure'.

catalysts.title: China continues to block inbound robotics/AI deals
catalysts.description: China's recent blocks on SoftBank/ABB and similar transactions indicate an ongoing pattern of rejecting foreign acquisitions in advanced robotics and AI sectors.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China Blocks $5.4 Billion SoftBank Robot Deal' and 'China blocks SoftBank’s takeover of ABB’s robotics division'.

catalysts.title: Regulatory snag on SK Hynix New York plans
catalysts.description: U.S. restrictions tied to China are delaying or complicating SK Hynix's planned New York chip investments, risking altered project scope or pauses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'SK Hynix's New York chip plans hit snag over US restrictions on China' — implying regulatory review and project delay.

catalysts.title: Western and private deals to diversify critical minerals
catalysts.description: Deals like Solvay's rare‑earths agreement indicate accelerated investment to reduce dependence on Chinese mineral supply, shifting sourcing patterns.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Solvay strikes rare earths deal that will reduce global dependence on China' and 'China expands overseas mining stakes'.

catalysts.title: US onshore chip production expansion (Texas plant)
catalysts.description: Reports of Samsung producing AMD/Nvidia parts at a second Texas plant signal near‑term expansion of US semiconductor fabrication and packaging capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Samsung to make AMD, Nvidia chip parts at second Texas plant, Maeil Business reports'.

catalysts.title: Data‑centre clients reduce China exposure
catalysts.description: Nvidia instructing data‑centre customers to cut China exposure will cause rapid vendor and sourcing changes across cloud and enterprise AI deployments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Nvidia orders data centre clients to reduce China exposure' and related reporting on supply shifts.

catalysts.title: UK policy moves and investment to reduce China minerals exposure
catalysts.description: MP warnings about UK exposure to Chinese mineral dominance are likely to spur policy actions and investments to secure alternative supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China’s critical minerals dominance leaves UK ‘dangerously exposed’, MPs warn' — likely policy response and investment.
